subject: Original Indev map settings (level type, shape, size, theme) for the project's Indev profile

projectIndevProfile.currentFixedOptions: type=island, theme=normal, 256x256x128 (Normal square), world border 256 centred on origin
projectIndevProfile.note: 20100223 is the LAST Indev build, so every original option below existed by then; Paradise and Woods were added 20100214, five days earlier.

primarySource.title: Indev map settings
primarySource.confidence: Wiki article with a HistoryTable of in-game changes; used as the option list. Dimensions are a published table, NOT read out of an original jar, and are recorded as such.

secondarySource.note: Confirms the feature list wording: 'Map generation screen with configurable map themes, map types, and map shapes', and lists the 20100223 latest version.

descriptions.Floating: multiple floating islands; death below as the surface is bedrock; floating gravel/sand common; water rare
descriptions.Flat: flat grass with flowers and trees plus a starting house
descriptions.Inland: slightly hilly; Island type with infinite flat land at the borders instead of water; sand and gravel common

levelTheme.introduced: Normal and Hell in Indev 0.31 20100107-1851; Paradise and Woods added 20100214

effects.Normal: sporadic trees; partly cloudy; equal day/night; all ores; lava near bedrock; boundary liquid water
effects.Hell: much less daylight so mobs spawn at any time; all water replaced by lava; dirt instead of grass; mushrooms abundant; farming one stage per day; boundary liquid lava
effects.Paradise: larger beaches and more flora; time always noon; hostile mobs only underground; farming 30-45 minutes per harvest; boundary liquid water
effects.Woods: constant overcast reducing light; higher tree density; spotty mushrooms; boundary liquid water

rules.Long: twice the length and half the width of a square map
rules.Deep: four times the height and half the width and length of a square map

upstreamMapping.record: mod.bluestaggo.modernerbeta.settings.component.FiniteLevelProperties(IndevType type, IndevTheme theme, int width, int length, int height)

levelTypeEnum.gap: There is NO 'flat' id. Upstream implements Island, Floating and Inland from the original list; 'classic' is Classic-era terrain, which is NOT the original Indev 'Flat' type. Flat is therefore unimplemented upstream and must not be presented as working.

themeEnum.match: Exactly the four original themes, and upstream ships one preset per theme: moderner_beta:indev, indev_hell, indev_paradise, indev_woods.

upstreamMapping.shapeAndSize: No shape or size enum: upstream collapses both into width/length/height, which the dimension table above supplies.

savedCustomSettings.note: Upstream's own per-world custom-settings mechanism, i.e. the supported place to persist a player's Indev choice for one world.

createWorldCustomisation.note: Upstream attaches its settings editor to world creation through vanilla's WorldCreationContext.Modifier. This project must use the same supported hook rather than assembling generator settings itself.

intendedBehaviour.scope: An Indev-era world creation may choose level type (Island/Floating/Inland), theme (Normal/Hell/Paradise/Woods) and shape+size (Square/Long/Deep x Small/Normal/Huge). Flat is listed but unavailable, with the reason shown, because upstream has no implementation.
intendedBehaviour.default: Island / Normal / Square Normal, which is what the project generates today, so an untouched flow creates exactly the same world as before.
intendedBehaviour.gating: Only profiles whose generator is the finite Indev provider offer these options; ordinary worlds, Infdev and every later version are unchanged.
intendedBehaviour.preservation: Existing Indev saves keep their stored settings; no retrofit, no chunk rewriting, no live generator swapping.
nonGoals: adding a second settings system alongside Moderner Beta's

openQuestions: Which hook our create-world flow uses to hand the chosen options to the new world: vanilla's WorldCreationContext.Modifier (what upstream uses) or a saved preset pack written for the world directory. To be settled by inspection in the implementation round, not guessed.
Whether the original 'Flat' type can be expressed at all through the pinned upstream provider; if not it stays visibly unavailable.
